title: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene (615712) on chromosome 5p15.2.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a heterozygous OTULIN variant causing ORAS-like disease.

checks.claim: The OTULIN gene is located on chromosome 5p15.2.
checks.evidence_quote: OTULIN+/del(5p-)
checks.explanation: The paper does not give the chromosomal location. This is standard nomenclature added by the draft, and the paper's reference to a 5p deletion is consistent with it.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is an OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS)-like disorder with onset in infancy. Its features include recurrent panniculitis, sterile neutrophilic skin inflammation with pathergy, necrotizing skin and soft tissue lesions, fever, edema, and markedly raised C-reactive protein (CRP) with neutrophilia. It is caused by a heterozygous dominant negative OTULIN variant that arose de novo, unlike the biallelic loss-of-function variants reported earlier in ORAS (Davidson et al., 2024).

checks.claim: AIPDSA is an OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS)-like disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We have demonstrated the mechanism by which a heterozygous variant in OTULIN can act in a dominant negative manner to cause an ORAS-like disease.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the condition an ORAS-like disease.

checks.claim: AIPDSA has onset in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: At 4 days old he developed peri-umbilical erythema and was diagnosed with a presumed abscess
checks.explanation: Onset was at 4 days of age in P1 and at 7 months in P2.

checks.evidence_quote: he developed repeated areas of swelling and erythema consistent with panniculitis
checks.explanation: P1 had recurrent panniculitis, and P2's skin biopsy also showed panniculitis.

checks.evidence_quote: developed lesions that were believed to represent pathergy, with sterile pustular abscesses forming at the sight of prior trauma
checks.explanation: The paper describes sterile pustular lesions with pathergy and neutrophilic inflammation.

checks.evidence_quote: both P1 and P2 suffered from necrotizing wounds that improved upon TNF blockade

checks.claim: AIPDSA features include fever.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with a fever (38–39°C) and generalized edema

checks.claim: AIPDSA features include edema.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with a fever (38–39°C) and generalized edema
checks.explanation: P2 had generalized edema, and P1 had extensive body edema.

checks.claim: AIPDSA features include markedly raised C-reactive protein (CRP) with neutrophilia.
checks.evidence_quote: Initial investigations showed significant leukocytosis (45.5 × 109/L) with neutrophilia (40.9 × 109/L), high CRP (264 mg/L)
checks.explanation: Both patients had raised CRP with neutrophilia.

checks.explanation: The variant was heterozygous, dominant negative and de novo in both patients.

checks.explanation: The paper states that all previously reported ORAS variants were biallelic loss of function.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) described a 22-month-old Caucasian boy (P1) with nonconsanguineous parents who was born at 31 weeks' gestation. At 4 days of age he developed periumbilical erythema with sterile neutrophilic inflammation around a urachal remnant. After surgery the wound dehisced and did not close, and he later developed a spontaneous cutaneous duodenal stoma. At 8 weeks of age he had an acute respiratory deterioration with body edema, hypotension, and presumed pulmonary edema, which responded to corticosteroids. Other features were recurrent panniculitis and pathergy with sterile pustular abscesses at injection and cannula sites. An echogenic focus on the tricuspid valve was treated as culture-negative endocarditis. Laboratory findings were raised CRP (100-200 mg/L), neutrophilia, monocytosis, eosinophilia, persistent thrombocytopenia, and initial hypogammaglobulinemia. A skin biopsy showed acute inflammatory exudate with suppuration and necrosis.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) also described a Saudi girl (P2) born at term to nonconsanguineous parents. At 7 months of age, 2 weeks after routine vaccinations, she presented with fever, generalized edema, and multiple tender skin lesions. These progressed to cellulitis-like plaques and to necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration, which required debridement and fasciotomy. She had leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and a high CRP (264 mg/L). All cultures were negative, and biopsy showed infiltration by neutrophils and plasma cells with necrosis. At 12 months of age she had a second attack with fever, erythematous plaques, and a CRP of 393 mg/L, and a skin biopsy showed panniculitis. She responded promptly to corticosteroids.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) observed markedly increased transcription of IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF, in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from P1. P1's fibroblasts had a raised interferon-stimulated gene score. This score was similar to that of fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS and higher than that of fibroblasts from healthy donors or from OTULIN-haploinsufficient individuals. THP-1 monocytes stably expressing C129S OTULIN showed a similar inflammatory gene signature, whereas those expressing wildtype OTULIN did not.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous dominant negative OTULIN variant reported by Davidson et al. (2024) arose de novo in 2 unrelated individuals, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. This contrasts with the biallelic loss-of-function OTULIN variants reported earlier in ORAS.

checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up testing on P2’s parents confirmed the de novo nature of the variant
checks.explanation: The variant was de novo in both P1 and P2, who were unrelated.

checks.claim: The de novo occurrence of the heterozygous OTULIN variant in AIPDSA is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: The paper does not use the term 'autosomal dominant', but this follows directly from a de novo heterozygous dominant negative variant.

checks.claim: Biallelic loss-of-function OTULIN variants were reported earlier in ORAS, in contrast to the heterozygous variant in AIPDSA.
checks.evidence_quote: To date, all reported ORAS-associated variants have been biallelic loss of function

paragraphs.text: In P1, the Caucasian boy, trio exome sequencing by Davidson et al. (2024) identified a de novo heterozygous c.386G-C transversion in the OTULIN gene, resulting in a cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution. The variant was absent from gnomAD. Cys129 lies in the catalytic domain and is essential for OTULIN enzymatic activity.

paragraphs.text: In functional studies, Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S OTULIN was as thermostable as wildtype OTULIN, and that levels of OTULIN and of the LUBAC components were normal in patient fibroblasts. However, the mutant protein failed to hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin. An activity-based probe showed that active wildtype and inactive C129S OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in patient fibroblasts. Surface plasmon resonance showed that C129S OTULIN bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity. M1-linked ubiquitin chains accumulated in patient fibroblasts. HEK293T cells express endogenous OTULIN, and transfecting them with C129S OTULIN caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation. Wildtype OTULIN and the loss-of-function variants Y244C and N341D did not have these effects. C129S OTULIN drove NF-kappa-B activity even when cotransfected with wildtype OTULIN at lower ratios, indicating a dominant negative effect.

checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN exhibited equivalent protein stability with similar melting temperature to wild type (WT) OTULIN in a Tycho NT.6 assay

checks.evidence_quote: we did not observe a consistent decrease in transcription or protein expression of any LUBAC component (SHARPIN, HOIP, or HOIL-1) in patient fibroblasts compared with HD
checks.explanation: OTULIN expression was also similar to healthy donors. Only P1's fibroblasts were studied.

checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN, like the previously reported C129A mutation, failed to hydrolyze M1–di-Ub in a cell-free cleavage assay

checks.explanation: Matches the paper. Only P1's fibroblasts were tested.

checks.explanation: WT and Y244C were tested for M1-Ub accumulation, but N341D was tested only in the NF-kB luciferase assay. The paper therefore does not show that N341D failed to cause M1-Ub accumulation.

checks.evidence_quote: cotransfection of WT and C129S OTULIN into HEK 293T cells across a range of ratios revealed that C129S OTULIN was able to drive NFκB activity even at lower concentrations than WT OTULIN

checks.claim: The OTULIN C129S variant has a dominant negative effect.
checks.evidence_quote: Collectively, these data indicate C129S OTULIN has a dominant negative effect over WT OTULIN

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) found that fibroblasts from patients with the C129S variant were as sensitive to TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death as fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS. They were more sensitive than fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients or healthy donors. The cell death was mainly apoptotic: caspase inhibition reduced it, and necrostatin-1 had little effect. TNF-induced MAPK and NF-kappa-B signaling and IL-6/IL-8 secretion were largely normal in patient fibroblasts.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) found that fibroblasts from patients with OTULIN C129S were as sensitive to TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death as fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN patient fibroblasts died at a similar rate to OTULIN biallelic loss-of-function fibroblasts

checks.claim: Fibroblasts from patients with OTULIN C129S were more sensitive to TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death than fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients or healthy donors.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S heterozygous OTULIN and ORAS fibroblasts exhibited markedly increased sensitivity to TNF-induced cell death compared with HD and OTULIN-haploinsufficent cells

checks.claim: TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts was mainly apoptotic.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S heterozygous OTULIN patient fibroblasts die primarily by apoptosis and, to a lesser extent, by necroptosis in response to TNF+CHX stimulation

checks.claim: Caspase inhibition reduced TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: Treatment with the pan caspase inhibitor QVD significantly reduced TNF-CHX–induced cell death in the C129S heterozygous and ORAS lines

checks.claim: Necrostatin-1 had little effect on TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: while the RIPK1 kinase inhibitor, necrostatin-1 (Nec-1), had minimal effect

checks.claim: TNF-induced MAPK and NF-kappa-B signaling were largely normal in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: this data demonstrates that C129S OTULIN heterozygosity does not significantly alter MAPK or NFκB signaling in response to TNF stimulation in patient fibroblasts

checks.claim: TNF-induced IL-6/IL-8 secretion was largely normal in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: secretion of the inflammatory cytokines: IL-8 and IL-6 in response to TNF stimulation was comparable between C129S OTULIN heterozygous, OTULIN-haploinsufficent (Spaan et al., 2022), and HD fibroblast lines

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN binds LUBAC. In cells it promoted ubiquitination of the LUBAC component SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP. Patient fibroblasts showed increased OTULIN-LUBAC interaction, and most of the OTULIN bound to LUBAC was catalytically inactive. Patient cells also showed reduced recruitment of HOIP and SHARPIN to the TNFR1 signaling complex and reduced modification of RIPK1. The authors concluded that M1-ubiquitin accumulating on LUBAC reduces its recruitment to TNFR1 and promotes TNF-induced cell death, leading to necrotizing tissue.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN binds LUBAC.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, in cells, C129S OTULIN can bind to LUBAC and facilitate autoubiquitination of the complex

checks.claim: In cells, C129S OTULIN promoted ubiquitination of the LUBAC component SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP.
checks.evidence_quote: SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP immunoprecipitated with C129S OTULIN were more heavily ubiquitinated compared with the HOIP and SHARPIN pulled down by WT OTULIN

checks.claim: Fibroblasts from OTULIN C129S patients showed increased OTULIN-LUBAC interaction.
checks.evidence_quote: We observed a marked increased interaction of OTULIN and LUBAC in patient fibroblasts compared with HD

checks.claim: In OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts, most of the OTULIN bound to LUBAC was catalytically inactive.
checks.evidence_quote: we confirmed that in C129S OTULIN patient cells, the majority of OTULIN bound to the LUBAC complex is catalytically inactive

checks.claim: OTULIN C129S patient cells showed reduced recruitment of HOIP and SHARPIN to the TNFR1 signaling complex.
checks.evidence_quote: we observed reduced recruitment of LUBAC components SHARPIN and HOIP to the TNFR1 signaling complex in patient cells compared with HD

checks.claim: OTULIN C129S patient cells showed reduced modification of RIPK1.
checks.evidence_quote: we observed consistently less modification of RIPK1 in patient cells

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) concluded that M1-ubiquitin accumulating on LUBAC reduces LUBAC recruitment to TNFR1 and promotes TNF-induced cell death, leading to necrotizing tissue.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, C129S OTULIN heterozygosity leads to accumulation of M1-Ub chains on LUBAC complexes, which reduces LUBAC recruitment to the TNFR1 signaling complex. Decreased LUBAC recruitment promotes TNF-induced cell death, which contributes to the key feature of the ORAS-like disease, necrotizing tissue.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both patients responded to corticosteroids. In P1, adalimumab allowed the steroid dose to be reduced, lowered CRP, and supported wound healing; ruxolitinib was also tried, but its benefit was unclear. P2 was treated with infliximab plus methotrexate, was weaned off steroids, and remained in remission for 2 years. Prophylactic antibiotics improved wound healing in P1 and controlled recurrent chest infections in P2.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both AIPDSA patients P1 and P2 responded to corticosteroids.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with the abdominal wound healing, these lesions were responsive to corticosteroids.
checks.explanation: P2 also showed prompt improvement after starting corticosteroids.

checks.claim: In AIPDSA patient P1, adalimumab allowed the steroid dose to be reduced.
checks.evidence_quote: he was treated with TNF-blockade (Adalimumab), which seemed to improve the rate of healing allowing for a reduced steroid dose

checks.claim: In AIPDSA patient P1, adalimumab lowered CRP and supported wound healing.
checks.evidence_quote: Blockade of TNF signaling dramatically reduced CRP levels and promoted a decrease in numbers of circulating myeloid cells in P1 (Fig. 1 D). Furthermore, Adalimumab therapy supported abdominal wound healing in P1.

checks.claim: Ruxolitinib was tried in AIPDSA patient P1, but its benefit was unclear.
checks.evidence_quote: the JAK inhibitor Ruxolitinib was also trialed in P1. However, P1’s discontinuous bowel wound may impede absorption, so the exact benefit of this drug is currently unknown

checks.claim: AIPDSA patient P2 was treated with infliximab plus methotrexate and was weaned off steroids.
checks.evidence_quote: the patient was started on anti-TNF (Infliximab) with adjunctive Methotrexate, and corticosteroid was successfully weaned off

checks.claim: AIPDSA patient P2 remained in remission for 2 years on infliximab plus methotrexate.
checks.evidence_quote: she remains in clinical and biochemical remission since starting anti-TNF therapy, and she completed her third year of life in June 2023, achieving 2 years of disease remission

checks.claim: Prophylactic antibiotics improved wound healing in AIPDSA patient P1.
checks.evidence_quote: the rate of healing was noted to be remarkably better when he was covered with broad-spectrum antibiotic prophylaxis

checks.claim: Prophylactic antibiotics controlled recurrent chest infections in AIPDSA patient P2.
checks.evidence_quote: Initially, she had recurrent simple chest infections, which notably improved after adding prophylactic antibiotics.

clinical_synopsis.feature: acute respiratory deterioration with pulmonary edema

allelic_variants.name: OTULIN, CYS129SER
allelic_variants.phenotype: Autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome, autosomal dominant

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) studied 2 unrelated patients with AIPDSA and found the same cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution in the catalytic domain of OTULIN in both, caused by 2 different nucleotide changes. In a Caucasian boy (P1), trio exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous c.386G-C transversion, which was absent from gnomAD. In a Saudi girl (P2), whole-genome sequencing identified a heterozygous c.385T-A transversion, and parental testing confirmed it was de novo.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) studied 2 unrelated patients with AIPDSA.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.

checks.claim: Both unrelated AIPDSA patients had the same cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution in OTULIN, caused by 2 different nucleotide changes.
checks.evidence_quote: a variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A, which results in the same cysteine to serine change at position 129, was identified
checks.explanation: P1 carried c.386G>C and P2 carried c.385T>A; both give C129S.

checks.claim: The OTULIN C129S substitution is in the catalytic domain of OTULIN.
checks.evidence_quote: cysteine 129 is part of the OTULIN catalytic domain

checks.claim: Trio exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous OTULIN c.386G-C transversion in a Caucasian boy with AIPDSA (P1).
checks.evidence_quote: Trio exome sequencing was performed on P1 and his parents; this identified a de novo variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.386G>C

checks.claim: The OTULIN c.386G-C variant was absent from gnomAD.
checks.evidence_quote: absent from databases of normal variation, including gnomAD (v2.1.1 and v3.1.2)

checks.claim: Whole-genome sequencing identified a heterozygous OTULIN c.385T-A transversion in a Saudi girl with AIPDSA (P2).
checks.evidence_quote: P2 underwent whole genome sequencing and a variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A

checks.claim: Parental testing confirmed that the OTULIN c.385T-A variant in AIPDSA patient P2 was de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up testing on P2’s parents confirmed the de novo nature of the variant

paragraphs.text: In functional studies, Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S OTULIN was thermostable but could not hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin, although it still bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity. Active wildtype and inactive C129S OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in patient fibroblasts, and M1-linked ubiquitin chains accumulated in these cells. In HEK293T cells, C129S OTULIN caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation, even when cotransfected with wildtype OTULIN at lower ratios. These findings indicated a dominant negative effect.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S OTULIN was thermostable.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN exhibited equivalent protein stability with similar melting temperature to wild type (WT) OTULIN

checks.claim: C129S OTULIN could not hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN, like the previously reported C129A mutation, failed to hydrolyze M1–di-Ub in a cell-free cleavage assay

checks.claim: C129S OTULIN bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity.
checks.evidence_quote: we confirmed C129S OTULIN similarly binds to M1–di-Ub with high affinity

checks.claim: Active wildtype and inactive C129S OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in AIPDSA patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: both WT (active) and C129S (inactive) forms of OTULIN are coexpressed in seemingly equal amounts

checks.claim: M1-linked ubiquitin chains accumulated in OTULIN C129S patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: we observed significant accumulation of M1-Ub chains in patient cells compared with HD fibroblasts

checks.claim: In HEK293T cells, C129S OTULIN caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation.
checks.evidence_quote: transient transfection of human embryonic kidney (HEK) 293T cells with C129S OTULIN triggered M1-Ub chain accumulation

checks.claim: In HEK293T cells, C129S OTULIN caused dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation, even when cotransfected with wildtype OTULIN at lower ratios.
checks.evidence_quote: C129S OTULIN was able to drive NFκB activity even at lower concentrations than WT OTULIN
checks.explanation: The dose-dependence is stated separately in the paper.

checks.claim: The OTULIN C129S variant has a dominant negative effect.
checks.evidence_quote: these data indicate C129S OTULIN has a dominant negative effect over WT OTULIN
